title: Add a contact in the classic interface
aliases: create a contact in the old Contacts tab
body:
Archived: this article describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025. See the current article for the new layout.

In classic Harbour CRM, contacts were added from the old Contacts tab.

1. Click the **Contacts** tab on the left-hand menu.
2. Click the green **Add Contact** button above the list.
3. Fill in **First Name**, **Last Name** and **Email** in the pop-up window.
4. Click **Save & Close**, or **Save & Add Another** to enter several people in a row.

In the classic version the **Company** field was a plain text box, so linked companies had to be matched later by an administrator.

title: Update a contact's phone number (classic)
aliases: edit phone in old contact page
body:
Archived: describes the classic editor, retired in March 2025.

To change a contact's phone number in the classic editor:

1. Open the old **Contacts** tab and click the contact's name.
2. Click **Edit Contact** in the grey toolbar.
3. Find the **Phone (Primary)** box and type the new number. Classic did not add country codes automatically, so include the + sign.
4. Click **Update**.

A second number could be stored in **Phone (Alt)**. Changes were not logged in the contact's history in the classic version, which is why some older accounts have no record of who edited a number.

title: Change a contact's email (classic)
body:
Archived: this article describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.

1. Open the old **Contacts** tab.
2. Click the contact, then **Edit Contact**.
3. Type the new address into the **Email** box. Classic accepted only one address per contact.
4. Click **Update**.

If the old address was on a mailing list, you also needed to open **Lists** and remove it by hand, because classic did not sync the two. Duplicate email warnings did not exist, so two contacts could share the same address without any message.

title: Delete a contact (classic)
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

Deleting a contact in the classic version was immediate and could not be reversed.

1. Open the old **Contacts** tab.
2. Tick the box beside one or more contacts.
3. Click **Actions** > **Delete Selected**.
4. Click **OK** on the grey warning box.

No recycle bin existed. Any open deals showed the contact name in plain text but were no longer linked. Classic accounts needed to contact support within 7 days to ask for a backup restore, a policy that no longer applies.

title: Export contacts to CSV (classic)
body:
Archived: describes the classic export, retired in March 2025.

1. Click the **Contacts** tab.
2. Click **Tools** in the top right and choose **Export to CSV**.
3. Classic always exported every contact and every column; there was no filter.
4. Click **Generate File**. A link appeared under **Tools** > **My Downloads** after a few minutes and stayed for 48 hours.

Custom fields were placed at the end of the file with their internal names, such as cf_1042, rather than their labels. Exports were limited to 10,000 rows.

title: Link a contact to a company (classic)
aliases: connect contact to company old interface
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

In classic, the link between a contact and a company was set from the company side.

1. Open the **Accounts** tab (the old name for Companies).
2. Click the company name.
3. Scroll to **Related Contacts** and click **Link Existing**.
4. Tick one or more contacts and click **Add**.

The **Company** box on the contact page was only a text label and did not create a link. Today you can link directly from the contact's page.

title: Add a company (classic Accounts tab)
body:
Archived: this article describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.

Companies were called Accounts in the classic version.

1. Click the **Accounts** tab.
2. Click **New Account**.
3. Type the **Account Name**. Also fill in **Phone**, **Web** and **Billing Street** if you have them.
4. Choose an **Account Owner** from the drop-down.
5. Click **Save**.

Classic had no website lookup. Logos could only be uploaded manually on the edit page.

title: Edit a company's phone, website or address (classic)
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

1. Open the **Accounts** tab and click the company.
2. Click **Edit** in the grey toolbar.
3. Change **Phone**, **Web** or the address fields **Street**, **City**, **State** and **Postcode**. Each part of the address was a separate box.
4. Click **Save**.

The website was not checked, so entries like www.example needed the full http:// to be clickable. Contacts linked to the account did not pick up the new address; they had their own address fields.

title: Create a deal (classic pipeline)
body:
Archived: describes the classic pipeline, retired in March 2025.

1. Click the **Pipeline** tab.
2. Click **+ Add Opportunity** at the top of the first column.
3. Enter the **Opportunity Name** and **Value**.
4. Search for the **Contact**. The company is filled in from the contact.
5. Click **Save**.

Classic called deals opportunities and only supported one pipeline. The **Close Date** was optional, which meant reports often showed gaps.

title: Mark a deal as won or lost (classic)
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

1. In the **Pipeline** tab, click the opportunity card.
2. Click **Change Status**.
3. Choose **Closed Won** or **Closed Lost**.
4. For **Closed Lost**, type a reason in the free-text **Notes** box. Classic had no reason list.
5. Click **OK**.

Closed cards disappeared from the board and could only be found by filtering the list view with **Show Closed**. There was no Reopen button; support had to reopen them.

title: Move a deal to another stage (classic Kanban)
body:
Archived: this article describes the classic Kanban board, retired in March 2025.

1. Open the **Pipeline** tab.
2. Click and hold the opportunity card.
3. Drag it onto the next column header and release.
4. A box asks for a **Stage Note**. Click **Skip** if not needed.

On laptops without a mouse, open the card, click **Edit** and use the **Stage** drop-down instead. Classic could not skip over locked stages, and there was no keyboard method. The board showed a maximum of 50 cards per column.

title: Create a custom field (Settings > Legacy)
body:
Archived: describes Settings > Legacy, retired in March 2025.

1. Click the cog icon, then **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Field Manager**.
2. Choose the module: **Contacts**, **Accounts** or **Opportunities**.
3. Click **Create Field**.
4. Enter a **Field Name** and choose a **Data Type**: Text, Number, Date or Pick List.
5. Click **Save**.

Classic allowed up to 25 custom fields per module. New fields only showed on records after the user refreshed the browser.

title: Rename a custom field (classic Field Manager)
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Field Manager**.
2. Select the module and find the field.
3. Click the **Edit** link at the end of the row.
4. Change the **Field Name**.
5. Click **Save**.

Renaming in classic did not update saved reports or filters that used the old name; they showed an empty column until someone rebuilt them. This limitation is the reason many clients kept the old name and added a description instead.

title: Delete a custom field (classic)
body:
Archived: describes Settings > Legacy, retired in March 2025.

1. Open **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Field Manager**.
2. Find the field for the right module.
3. Click **Delete** at the end of the row.
4. Click **Yes, delete** on the warning.

Values were wiped immediately from every record and could not be restored. Deleting a field used by a saved report caused that report to show an error until it was edited. Only users with the **Super Admin** role could delete fields in classic.

title: Change your client contact number (classic account page)
aliases: update our business phone old settings
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

In classic Harbour CRM, the client is the business using the CRM, and its number was kept on the old My Account page.

1. Click your name at the top right and choose **My Account**.
2. Open the **Company Profile** section.
3. Edit **Primary Phone**.
4. Click **Update Profile**.

Changes needed a support ticket if the account had more than one **Super Admin**. No verification code was sent. This number is different from any contact's phone number.

title: Change the billing email (classic)
aliases: update invoice email for subscription old
body:
Archived: describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.

1. Click your name and choose **My Account**.
2. Open **Plan & Billing**.
3. Click **Change** next to **Invoice Email**.
4. Enter the new address and click **Save**.

In classic the receipts for the whole account went to this single address, and there was no confirmation link. Because of that, some accounts discovered missed receipts months later. The newer Billing page supports additional recipients and a verification email.

title: Change currency (classic Settings > Legacy)
body:
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Localisation**.
2. Choose a value from **Base Currency**.
3. Click **Apply**.

Changing the base currency in classic recalculated every opportunity value using that day's exchange rate, which surprised many clients. This is no longer the behaviour: amounts are left unchanged. Classic also required you to log out and back in before the new currency symbol appeared.

title: Reset your password (classic sign-in page)
body:
Archived: describes the classic sign-in page, retired in March 2025.

1. On the old sign-in page, click **Trouble signing in?** under the password box.
2. Type your username. In classic this was often not your email address.
3. Click **Email Me**.
4. Follow the link, which expired after 24 hours, and enter a password of at least 8 characters.

Passwords from classic were accepted without symbols or numbers. Everyone has since been asked to update to the newer 12-character rule.

title: Lead scoring (retired feature)
body:
Archived: this feature was retired in March 2025 along with the classic interface.

Lead scoring gave each contact a number of points based on activity.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Scoring Rules**.
2. Click **New Rule**.
3. Choose an event such as **Email opened** (+2) or **Form submitted** (+10).
4. Click **Save Rule**.

Scores appeared in a **Score** column on the old Contacts tab. Existing scores were not carried over to the new interface. Use deal stages and tags to prioritise contacts instead.

title: Data retention policy for deleted records (pre-2025)
aliases: how long are deleted contacts kept
body:
Archived: superseded policy. Retention changed after March 2025.

Under the previous policy, records deleted from your Harbour CRM were kept in system backups for 7 days and then removed. During that period, the client's account owner could ask support to restore them.

Requests had to be made from the client's registered billing email, and restoration was a full-account restore, not a single contact. Because of that, anything created after the backup time was lost.

This policy does not apply to accounts migrated to the new interface. Please see the current article on deleting contacts for the timeframes that apply today.

title: Import contacts (classic importer)
body:
Archived: classic importer, retired in March 2025.

1. Click **Tools** > **Import Contacts**.
2. Click **Choose File** and select a CSV. XLSX files were not supported.
3. Click **Next** and match each column header to a field. Headers had to match exactly or be mapped by hand.
4. Click **Run Import**.

Classic created a duplicate whenever an email already existed, and there was no undo. The recommended trick was to export first, then import into a test account. Imports over 5,000 rows were split by support.

title: Using the Tasks tab (retired)
body:
Archived: the Tasks tab was retired in March 2025.

In the classic interface, follow-ups were kept in a separate Tasks tab.

1. Click **Tasks** in the left menu.
2. Click **New Task**.
3. Type a **Subject**, choose a **Due Date** and link the task to a contact with **Related To**.
4. Click **Save**.

Overdue tasks were shown in red. Tasks are now created from the contact or deal itself under **Activities**, and existing tasks were migrated automatically. Recurring tasks were not supported in classic.

title: Generate a legacy API key
body:
Archived: legacy API keys stopped working in June 2025.

1. Click the cog icon and choose **Settings** > **Legacy** > **API Access**.
2. Click **Generate Key**.
3. Copy the key immediately. It was shown only once.
4. Use it as the **X-Harbour-Key** header on your requests.

Legacy keys had full access to everything in the client's account and could not be limited. They have been replaced by scoped tokens. Anyone still using an old key must create a new token and update their connected tools.

title: Two-step sign-in by text message (retired)
body:
Archived: SMS codes were retired in March 2025 for security reasons.

Classic accounts could receive a six-digit code by text message.

1. Open **My Account** > **Security**.
2. Click **Enable Text Verification**.
3. Enter your mobile number and click **Send Code**.
4. Type the code and click **Confirm**.

The number used was the sign-in user's own mobile, not the client contact number in company settings. If you still see this setting, switch to an authenticator app as described in the current security articles.

title: Update an employee's phone number (classic)
body:
Archived: describes the classic People directory, retired in 2025.

1. Click **Staff Directory** in the left menu.
2. Click the employee's name.
3. Click the **Edit** pencil on the **Contact Info** card.
4. Change **Mobile** or **Work Phone**.
5. Click **Save**.

In the classic version only the **HR Admin** role could change numbers; employees saw their own details as read-only. Numbers were shown in the staff directory to everyone, a setting that is now optional.

title: Request leave (classic form)
body:
Archived: classic leave form, retired in 2025.

1. Click **My Leave** and then **Request Leave**.
2. Pick a **Leave Type** from the list.
3. Type the **From** and **To** dates in DD/MM/YYYY format.
4. Add a reason in the **Comments** box.
5. Click **Submit Request**.

Your manager received an email with Approve and Decline links. Half days could only be entered by writing 0.5 in the **Days** box. The calendar view did not exist in classic.

title: Add an employee (classic wizard)
body:
Archived: the three-step wizard was retired in 2025.

1. Click **Staff Directory** then **Add Employee**.
2. Step 1: enter **Name**, **Email** and **Start Date**.
3. Step 2: choose **Department** and **Manager**.
4. Step 3: tick the **Welcome email** box if you want the invitation sent.
5. Click **Finish**.

Bank details and tax numbers could not be entered at this point; they were added later by a second administrator. The new onboarding checklist replaces this process.

title: Send an invoice reminder (classic)
body:
Archived: describes the classic invoice list, retired in 2025.

1. Click **Sales** > **Invoice List**.
2. Tick the overdue invoices, shown with a red date.
3. Click **Send Reminder**.
4. A fixed message is shown. The text could only be edited by an administrator in **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Email Text**.
5. Click **Send**.

Reminders could not be scheduled in advance. Customers saw a plain email with the invoice attached as a PDF and no online payment link.

title: Create an invoice (classic editor)
aliases: make a new invoice old editor
body:
Archived: classic invoice editor, retired in 2025.

1. Click **Sales** > **New Invoice**.
2. Choose the customer from the **Bill To** drop-down.
3. Click **Add Line** for each product or service and enter **Description**, **Qty** and **Price**.
4. Tick **Tax Inclusive** if prices already include tax.
5. Click **Save Draft** or **Approve & Send**.

The classic editor had no autosave, so closing the window lost your work. Invoice numbers could not be changed after approval.

title: Refund policy for Harbour Invoicing payments (old)
aliases: how long do refunds take previously
body:
Archived: superseded policy, replaced January 2025.

Under the earlier policy, refunds of card payments taken through Harbour Invoicing had to be requested by raising a ticket with support, and only the full amount could be returned.

Refunds took up to 10 working days and the processing fee on the original payment was not returned.

Clients can now issue full or partial refunds themselves from the payment record, and the fee treatment is described in the current pricing terms. This article is kept for audit purposes and should not be used to answer current questions.

title: Change invoice currency (classic)
body:
Archived: describes Settings > Legacy, retired in 2025.

1. Click the cog icon and choose **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Business**.
2. Open the **Currency** drop-down.
3. Pick the currency and click **Save**.

Classic only allowed one currency per account, so every invoice, quote and statement changed at once. Invoices that were already approved kept their old symbol on the PDF but showed the new one on screen, which caused confusion. Create a separate account if you needed to bill in two currencies.

title: Create an email campaign (Classic editor)
body:
Archived: describes the Classic editor, retired in March 2025.

1. Click **Campaigns** > **Create** and choose **Classic Editor**.
2. Type a **Campaign Name** and **Subject**.
3. Select a list under **Send To**.
4. In the editor, use the toolbar to add text, images and buttons. Layouts were chosen from six fixed templates.
5. Click **Send Test**, then **Schedule** or **Send Now**.

The classic editor did not preview on mobile screens. Segments were not available; you had to build a separate list.

title: Add a subscriber (classic lists)
aliases: add someone to mailing list old
body:
Archived: classic Lists screen, retired in March 2025.

1. Click **Lists** and then the name of your list.
2. Click **Add Subscriber**.
3. Type the **Email Address** and, if you like, **First Name**.
4. Tick **They have given permission** to continue.
5. Click **Add**.

Subscribers added by hand were marked as **Manual**. Classic could not import from Harbour CRM contacts; you had to export and upload a CSV. The sync introduced in the new version removes that step.

title: Set up a sender domain (legacy DNS wizard)
body:
Archived: legacy wizard retired in 2025.

1. Go to **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Sender Domains**.
2. Click **Add Domain** and type yours.
3. Copy the two **TXT** records shown and add them in your DNS host.
4. Click **Check Records**. Verification could take up to 48 hours.

The wizard used a shared signing key, so reputation was shared with other clients. The current setup provides a unique key for each domain and lists the records with copy buttons.

title: Assign a ticket (classic Desk)
body:
Archived: describes the classic Desk inbox, retired in 2025.

1. Click **Inbox** and open the ticket.
2. In the header click the **Owner** name.
3. Choose an agent from the list. Teams were not available as owners.
4. Click **Set Owner**.

The agent was not told unless you ticked **Notify by email**. Assigning several tickets at once was done from the list with **Select All** and **Change Owner**, which applied to every ticket on the page, including ones you did not mean to select.

title: Create a ticket on behalf of a customer (classic)
aliases: log a support request old Desk
body:
Archived: classic Desk, retired in 2025.

1. Click **New Case** at the top of the **Inbox**.
2. Type the customer's email under **Requester**.
3. Enter a **Subject** and describe the issue.
4. Choose a **Priority** (Low, Normal or Urgent).
5. Click **Create & Close** or **Create & Open**.

Cases were the classic name for tickets. Attachments were limited to 5 MB. Customers did not receive a copy unless **Email requester** was ticked.

title: Service level targets (old policy)
body:
Archived: superseded, replaced in 2025.

Under the previous setup, Harbour Desk used one account-wide first-reply target. Go to **Settings** > **Legacy** > **Targets** and enter a number of hours.

The clock ran 24 hours a day, including weekends, and was not paused when a ticket was waiting for the customer. Breached cases turned red in the **Inbox**.

Business hours and separate targets by priority are now supported, so this article should not be used to describe how timers work today.

title: Create a project (classic)
body:
Archived: describes the classic Projects screen, retired in 2025.

1. Click **Projects** then **Start Project**.
2. Enter a **Title** and **Description**.
3. Pick a **Project Type**: Standard or Template-based.
4. Select members from the **Team** list.
5. Click **Create**.

Classic opened the project on the **List** tab; boards were added later. Colours and icons did not exist. The **Client Access** option shown in some older screenshots has been removed.

title: Add a task (classic task list)
body:
Archived: classic task list, retired in 2025.

1. Open the project and click the **Tasks** tab.
2. Click **+ Task** at the bottom of the list.
3. Type the **Task Name** and press **Enter**.
4. Click the row to open the side panel and set **Assignee** and **Due**.

Classic did not allow sub-tasks, and an assignee could only be one person. To split work, users created several tasks with similar names, which made reports hard to read.

title: Archive a finished project (classic)
body:
Archived: classic behaviour, retired in 2025.

1. Open **Projects** and find the project.
2. Click **Actions** > **Close Project**.
3. Choose whether to **Keep tasks visible** or **Hide tasks**.
4. Click **Confirm**.

Closed projects were moved to the **Closed** tab. They could be reopened only by a **Project Admin**. Time entries could not be added after closing, so unbilled hours had to be logged first.
